title: Two campaign disclosure settlements
question: What conduct did the Ethics Commission establish in the election records?
finding: A union-sponsored committee settled two mailer disclaimer violations. A separate committee settled filing violations involving three elections.
how: Read the final stipulated orders alongside their exhibits. The first committee identifies a union sponsor. The second is a separate organization connected to campaign funding in the committee records.
limits: These are campaign-finance enforcement outcomes. The orders do not attribute either settlement to lobbying, a government award or a payment to an official.

rows.party: Working Families for Hillary Ronen, sponsored by UNITE HERE Local 2
rows.finding: The union contributed $40,000 to the independent expenditure committee. Two 2016 election mailers lacked required contributor and candidate-independence disclaimers. The settlement imposed $2,000 for the two mailers and $175 for late filings.

rows.party: Progress San Francisco, its principal officer and its treasurer
rows.finding: This separate political committee qualified as a city committee. It timely reported $1,159,900 in contributions to the state but missed the required City filings during three elections in 2018–19. Its settlement covers 24 late contribution reports and one omitted contribution on a campaign statement.
